nodes.title:
The campaign form's Retry pattern is what runs (P7). campaign.draft {retry:{pattern|maxAttempts|gapsMin|retryOn}} stores policy.retry (campaigns/retry.ts); attempt.retry_per_ladder uses it whenever the campaign has one.
- Patterns: standard (3 calls, 2 h then 1 day), gentle (2 calls, 1 day), persistent (4 calls, 1 h, 4 h, 1 day, plus voicemail) and none.
- Bounds: 1 to 6 calls in all, gaps of 15 min to 3 days.
- Only busy, no_answer, switched_off, voicemail and short_call can retry. invalid, opt_out, wrong_party, completed, unknown and operator_block never do. Provider faults keep the service ladder.
- An erased or suppressed person is refused before the ladder runs, whatever the outcome.
- Each retry is a new attempt, so the dial gate (DND, window, consent, budgets) decides it again. Its time is clamped with the gate's own eligibility().
- Older campaigns without policy.retry keep the service ladder.
- The form's select used to set a budget preset that the form's own budgets then overrode, so it changed nothing.
nodes.rationale: Must-be audit item 4 (research/2026-10-24/must-be-audit/README.md): the Retry pattern select changed nothing.
nodes.reverse_if: Measured connect rates show a pattern hurting answer rates or complaint signals: then change its gaps, never the never-retry list.

nodes.title:
A callback time the caller states beats the retry ladder for that contact.
- After a CONV_CALLBACK call, calls.followups reads the time with statedCallback (calls/stated-time.ts): a mark_callback tool event's words first, then the caller's own lines, newest first. Hindi, English and Hinglish, Latin or Devanagari; clock, relative, weekday, and part of day with a day cue; 'after 6' reads as 18:00.
- It is clamped into the campaign's window and TRAI's hours with the gate's eligibility(), and stored on the new callback attempt as attempt.callback {statedAt, at, clamped, quote, conversationId, text}.
- The text reads 'Calling back Tue 6:10 pm, as they asked', or '..., the first time the calling hours allow after the time they asked'. It shows on the contact page (attempt.list callback_text, words never returned) and on the campaign page (campaign.get callbacks).
- A vague time ('baad mein', 'call me later', 'kal call karo', 'subah se busy') gives a note on the ended attempt and no schedule: never a guess.
- At most 2 stated callbacks per chain; after that a person follows up.
- Hand-off callbacks (target 'callback') stay a person's task in the hand-off queue, not an automatic dial, so the person is not called twice.
nodes.rationale: Must-be audit item 4: a stated callback time was never passed (followups.ts:58), so the call came back after +2 h.
nodes.reverse_if: Live calls show stated-time parsing errors above 5% on reviewed callbacks: then hold parsed times for review instead of auto-scheduling.

nodes.title:
On a callback dial, the memory brief starts with 'callback: they_asked_for=Wed 11:00 am (said today)': a shape, never their words.
- memory.brief takes an optional attemptId. The worker sends it only for kind 'callback' attempts.
- The note is added only when all of these hold: the attempt is in this workspace and for this contact; its stored quote is still an exact substring of a caller turn of that call; the transcript is not purged; and memory is on for the workspace and the agent.
- The transcript purge (retention or erasure) strips attempt.callback.quote, so the note disappears with the words.
nodes.rationale: Must-be audit item 4.3: the callback she makes should know it is the one they asked for, under memory's existing quote-and-permission rules.
nodes.reverse_if: The callback note is recited as a line on live calls: then move it out of the brief into a turn-policy flag.

nodes.title:
tests/campaigns-retry.test.ts 5/5:
(1) The parser: 11 timed phrases across Hindi, English, Hinglish and Devanagari; 5 vague phrases give a note; 3 opt-out or unrelated lines give nothing; a Devanagari quote is the whole line.
(2) The persistent pattern runs 1 h, 4 h, then 1 day, and the 4th call is refused. gentle does not retry after voicemail; invalid never retries; none never retries. A gap landing after 19:00 moves to the next morning's 10:00. campaign.draft stores the pattern, and campaign.get says it in words; maxAttempts 9 is refused.
(3) A stated 18:10 beats the 'none' pattern ('Calling back Tue 6:10 pm, as they asked'). 21:30 clamps to Wed 10:00, and the text says so. A Sunday request moves to Monday 10:00 (the campaign skips Sundays). A vague time schedules nothing and the note shows on attempt.list. The attempt list never returns the caller's words, and campaign.get lists the callback.
(4) An opt-out, a suppressed contact and an erased contact are never retried, not even with a stated time.
(5) End to end through calls.afterCall: 'kal subah 11 baje call karna' on Tue gives a callback attempt at Wed 11:00 IST; memory.brief for that attempt reads 'callback: they_asked_for=Wed 11:00 am (said …)'. An ordinary attempt and another workspace's contact get no note. After erasure and the purge, the quote is gone and the note is gone.
Also: calls.test.ts' stub of attempt.retry_per_ladder widened to the new optional fields; fresh-DB suite and browser flows (see the event).
nodes.method: node:test on throwaway Postgres 16, all modules (buildApp(pool, modules)), FakeRuntime and FakeTelephony; the dial gate is exercised by the existing campaigns tests

events.details:
Must-be audit item 4 (gap 14), built by the memory builder with sanctioned campaigns edits.
- The Retry pattern select runs a real per-campaign ladder (campaigns/retry.ts).
- Stated callback times beat it, clamped into the calling hours, shown on the contact and campaign pages; vague times leave a note.
- The callback dial's memory brief says it is the callback they asked for.
- Opt-outs and erased people never retry.
- Migration 0704 (attempt.callback).
Verified: tests/campaigns-retry.test.ts 5/5 plus the full fresh-DB suite.
Not verified:
- Parsing on real callers' speech; numbers and words outside the tested set (e.g. 'saade chhe', 'paune saat') are not read, so they give a note or nothing.
- The browser flow of the new select; the screen copy is checked by type only.
- A per-campaign override of the never-retry list (none, by design).
